text: Nigeria is located in ______ Africa.
explanation: Nigeria is in the West African sub-region.

text: The name 'Nigeria' was suggested by ______.
explanation: Flora Shaw (later Lugard's wife) coined the name.

text: The amalgamation of the Northern and Southern protectorates took place in ______.
explanation: Lord Lugard amalgamated the protectorates in 1914.

text: Nigeria gained independence on ______.
explanation: Independence from British rule was in 1960.

text: The first Prime Minister of Nigeria was ______.
explanation: Tafawa Balewa was the head of government at independence.

text: The first military Head of State in Nigeria was ______.
explanation: Aguiyi Ironsi took over after the 1966 coup.

text: The Nigerian Civil War started in ______.
explanation: The war began in 1967 and ended in 1970.

text: The Biafran side was led by ______.
explanation: Ojukwu led the secessionist state of Biafra.

text: Which of these was a powerful pre-colonial kingdom in Nigeria?
explanation: Oyo was a major Yoruba empire.

text: The Sokoto Caliphate was founded by ______.
explanation: He led the jihad that established the caliphate.

text: Mary Slessor is famous for ______.
explanation: She worked in Calabar to end twin infanticide.

text: The capital of Nigeria was moved from Lagos to Abuja in ______.
explanation: The movement was officially completed in 1991.

text: Who discovered the mouth of River Niger?
explanation: Richard and John Lander confirmed the mouth of the Niger.

text: The Aba Women's Riot took place in ______.
explanation: A major revolt against British taxation.

text: Nigeria became a Republic in ______.
explanation: Nigeria severed ties with the British monarchy in 1963.

text: The first Governor-General of Nigeria was ______.
explanation: Lugard oversaw the amalgamation.

text: The currency used in Nigeria before the Naira was ______.
explanation: Nigeria used the British Pound.

text: The June 12, 1993 election was won by ______.
explanation: Moshood Abiola won the annulled election.

text: The Nok culture is famous for ______.
explanation: Terracotta (baked clay) figures found in Kaduna state.

text: Queen Amina was a legendary ruler of ______.
explanation: Warrior Queen of Zazzau (Zaria).

text: Benin City is famous for its ______.
explanation: The Benin Bronzes are world-famous.

text: The first political party in Nigeria was ______.
explanation: Nigerian National Democratic Party formed in 1923.

text: Herbert Macaulay is known as the father of ______.
explanation: A pioneer of Nigerian nationalism.

text: The Kanem-Borno Empire was located in ______ Nigeria.
explanation: Around Lake Chad area.

text: Who stopped the Nigerian Civil War?
explanation: Gowon declared 'No Victor, No Vanquished'.

text: The first Executive President of Nigeria was ______.
explanation: Shagari ruled in the Second Republic (1979).

text: Nigeria currently has ______ states.
explanation: 36 states plus the FCT.

text: The traditional ruler of Ife is called ______.
explanation: The Ooni of Ife.

text: The traditional ruler of Sokoto is called ______.
explanation: The Sultan of Sokoto.

text: The Igbo women's riot of 1929 was against ______.
explanation: Against the imposition of taxes on women.

text: Jaja of Opobo was a ______.
explanation: A powerful merchant king in the Niger Delta.

text: The Berlin Conference of 1884/85 was to ______.
explanation: European powers divided Africa among themselves.

text: Which country colonized Nigeria?
explanation: Nigeria was a British colony.

text: The first newspaper in Nigeria was ______.
explanation: Published by Henry Townsend in Abeokuta.

text: The 2023 general election produced ______ as President.
explanation: Bola Tinubu won the 2023 election.

text: Samuel Ajayi Crowther was the first ______.
explanation: First African Anglican Bishop.

text: The Hausa city states were conquered by ______.
explanation: Dan Fodio's jihad established Fulani rule over Hausa states.

text: The main economic activity in pre-colonial Nigeria was ______.
explanation: Farming was the mainstay.

text: Trans-Saharan trade was between West Africa and ______.
explanation: Trade across the Sahara desert.

text: Mungo Park died at ______.
explanation: He drowned at Bussa falls.

text: The Royal Niger Company was a ______ company.
explanation: Instrumental in British colonization.

text: Who is on the ₦1000 note?
explanation: First two indigenous CBN governors.

text: The ancient city of Ile-Ife is in ______ state.
explanation: Located in Osun State.

text: Indirect Rule was introduced by ______.
explanation: Ruling through traditional institutions.

text: The first story building in Nigeria is in ______.
explanation: Built in Badagry in 1845.

text: Kainji Dam is on River ______.
explanation: Major hydroelectric dam on the Niger.

text: The longest river in Nigeria is ______.
explanation: River Niger runs through the country.

text: The confluence of River Niger and Benue is at ______.
explanation: They meet at Lokoja.

text: The civil war lasted for ______ months.
explanation: 30 months (July 1967 - Jan 1970).

text: Who formed the Unity Party of Nigeria (UPN)?
explanation: Awolowo's party in the Second Republic.

text: The first indigenous Governor-General was ______.
explanation: Zik succeeded the British Governor-General.

text: Which of these is a cash crop from colonial times?
explanation: Cocoa was a major export crop.

text: The slave trade was abolished in ______.
explanation: British abolition of the slave trade.

text: Badagry was a major port for ______.
explanation: Notorious slave port.

text: The NYSC was established in ______.
explanation: Established by Yakubu Gowon after the civil war.

text: Who moved the motion for independence in 1953?
explanation: Enahoro moved the motion for self-rule.

text: The Old Oyo Empire collapsed due to ______.
explanation: Conflict with the Fulani and internal strife.

text: Bayajidda legend is associated with ______.
explanation: Legendary ancestor of the Hausa states.

text: Oduduwa is the ancestor of the ______.
explanation: Progenitor of the Yoruba race.

text: The Nri Kingdom is associated with the ______.
explanation: Ancient Igbo civilization.

text: What does ECOWAS stand for?

options.A: Economic Community of West African States
options.B: East Community of West African States
options.C: Economic Council of West African States
options.D: European Community of West African States

explanation: Regional economic bloc.

text: Nigeria's first coup took place in ______.
explanation: Led by Chukwuma Nzeogwu.

text: Murtala Muhammed was assassinated in ______.
explanation: February 13, 1976.

text: The Interim National Government was led by ______.
explanation: Appointed after the 1993 annulment.

text: Democracy day in Nigeria is now celebrated on ______.
explanation: Changed to honor MKO Abiola.

text: Which of these is NOT a founding father of Nigeria?
explanation: Abacha was a military dictator much later.

text: The first TV station in Africa was ______.
explanation: Western Nigeria Television (1959).

text: Nigeria has ______ geopolitical zones.
explanation: NW, NE, NC, SW, SE, SS.

text: The highest military rank in the Army is ______.
explanation: Though rarely attained in Nigeria.

text: Who handed over power to civilian rule in 1999?
explanation: He facilitated the transition to the 4th Republic.
